claim.why_it_matters: Every other line of 6.3.1.3 carries the ║ box marker, and the boxed general formats on pages 290-293 (sign condition, NOT condition-1, combined and abbreviated combined conditions) carry ║/╔╚ markers inside the pre block, but the condition-name condition's general format does not. verdict.reasoning: Printed page 290 (VI-58): a single rectangle encloses all of 6.3.1.3, from the heading through the general format line 'condition-name-1' to the paragraph ending 'its associated conditional variable.' The box's left and right edges run unbroken past the general format. 6.3.1.4 Switch-Status Condition, whose format is also 'condition-name-1', sits outside any box. In the markdown, the heading and all four prose paragraphs of 6.3.1.3 carry the ║ marker, and the sign-condition format on the same page carries ╔║╚ markers inside its pre block. The 6.3.1.3 pre block, however, holds a bare 'condition-name-1' and is identical to the unboxed 6.3.1.4 block. In this transcription the box marker records level membership, and that is content. As transcribed, the format reads as unboxed (low-level) material. The claim quotes both sources accurately. The practical impact is small because the boxed heading already places the section in the high level.
